spec_match.rationale: The dependency the removal rests on — a fenced frame can only be pointed at a FencedFrameConfig, and a config can only come from an auction or Shared Storage — is taken from the fenced frame specification and the intent thread, and every claim about it is checked by calling the API rather than by citing it. The three-stage rollout table follows the intent's own numbering.

interactive.rationale: A route census that calls five APIs for real, a live attach-and-measure comparison against an ordinary iframe, a runtime enumeration of Fence.prototype with a per-method call button, a four-context sweep using real frames, a six-way detection matrix, and an ad slot that renders through either branch with a switch to force the fallback.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Each card names the measurement its page performs, and each page performs exactly that measurement.

edge_cases.rationale: The createElement-is-always-truthy trap is demonstrated rather than asserted; window.fence being null rather than undefined is called out, along with why the two obvious checks disagree; the version-sniffing candidate is graded unreliable because Chrome 155 rolls the removal out behind a field trial; and the sandboxed opaque-origin context is swept to show the value depends on frame kind, not origin.

references.rationale: ChromeStatus, the WICG specification, Chrome for Developers documentation, and the blink-dev intent thread the removal plan comes from.

conformance.rationale: Four assertions, all side-effect free and all true on both sides of the removal: createElement never returning null, an unregistered tag becoming HTMLUnknownElement, the interface object and the config property agreeing, and no script-exposed config constructor. 4 pass / 0 fail on all four pages.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Driven on Chrome 150.0.7871.128 over CDP. Recorded: all five config routes present and all five refusing — an https-seller TypeError from runAdAuction, an addModule OperationError from selectURL, undefined from deprecatedReplaceInURN, an illegal-constructor TypeError from FencedFrameConfig, and a conversion TypeError from assigning a plain object to config; an attached fencedframe measured at 260x90 with window.length unchanged, contentWindow undefined and config null against an iframe measured at 260x90 with window.length incremented and a real content window; Fence.prototype declaring three methods, all of which throw on a null receiver; window.fence null in the top document, a same-origin frame and a sandboxed frame; and the slot rendering through the iframe branch both when no config was available and when the element was forced out of consideration.

telemetry_health.rationale: One namespaced console line per action. No errors or unhandled rejections: every speculative call is awaited inside a try/catch and its message is printed into the page rather than thrown.

design_system.rationale: Shared stylesheet and tokens throughout, including the embedded slot document, house stage/table/verdict patterns, inline SVG rather than emoji.

accessibility.rationale: Buttons with visible labels and 44px minimum targets, a checkbox label whose hit area meets the same minimum, titles on every frame the pages create, role=status with aria-live on each verdict and log, captions and scoped headers on every table, and explicit focus-visible outlines. The hidden probe frames are aria-hidden and clipped rather than display:none so they still run.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Tables scroll inside their own containers, the slot and comparison frames are max-width constrained rather than fixed, and the button rows wrap.

openQuestions.title: No config was ever obtained, so the fenced-frame branch is never taken
openQuestions.detail: The route census, the slot renderer and the context sweep all agree that no config is available, which is the correct result for this browser and this origin but means the fenced-frame rendering path is never exercised anywhere in the feature. Reaching it would need an https origin, Privacy Sandbox enrollment, a decision-logic worklet and a registered interest group on a Chrome earlier than 152 — a piece of infrastructure rather than a page, and one with a closing window.

openQuestions.title: The post-removal state is predicted, not observed
openQuestions.detail: Chrome 150 is before all three stages, so the pages state what each check will report afterwards without having seen it. The predictions follow from the DOM specification rather than from the intent's prose, and the assertions are written to hold on both sides — but the first 155 build to hand should be used to re-drive every page and check the predicted column against the observed one.

openQuestions.title: deprecatedReplaceInURN returns undefined rather than refusing
openQuestions.detail: Included in the census because it was part of the same surface, it resolves to undefined instead of throwing, which the table reports verbatim as "not a config". Whether that is a deliberate stub or simply what it always did for an unknown urn is not something this page establishes.

guidanceConsulted: modern-web-guidance: interactive over static, evidence over assertion
AGENTS.md: for removals and deprecations, pair detection with a working replacement pattern
summary: A removal shown as an argument you can check: count the ways into the element, find zero, then measure what an element nothing can fill still costs a page. The migration concept turns that into the pattern that survives all three stages — ask for the config, not for the element — and grades six detection candidates against what each will report once the tag is gone.
